title: Engineering tunable $p$-wave magnetism in antiferromagnetic bilayers
authors: Yu-Han Lin, Jin-Wei Dong, Ziqiang Wang, Sen Zhou
abstract: We propose a symmetry-guided route to engineer tunable $p$-wave magnetism in a bilayer system composed of two AB-stacked antiferromagnetic square lattices with their collinear moments nonparallel to each other. We show that an in-plane relative shift between the two layers selectively breaks the symmetries protecting spin degeneracy while preserving time-reversal-related constraints, thereby generating odd-parity spin splitting in a fully compensated magnetic state without spin-orbit coupling. The direction and the magnitude of the resulting $p$-wave spin-splitting, together with the associated spin responses, can be continuously tuned by the in-plane displacement, providing a potential knob for control. We further map the bilayer system onto an effective bond-modulated square lattice and investigate the corresponding Hubbard model within a mean-field framework. The calculated phase diagram reveals extended regions where $p$-wave magnetism with coplanar or chiral spin textures emerges spontaneously. Our results establish a minimal equilibrium platform for realizing and manipulating $p$-wave magnetism in two-dimensional systems.
summary: This work proposes a symmetry-controlled method to realize and manipulate p-wave magnetism in an antiferromagnetic bilayer system using only an in-plane relative shift between the layers. By analyzing the system via a Hubbard model, the authors demonstrate that this geometric displacement continuously tunes the p-wave spin splitting and associated spin responses, providing a clean, equilibrium platform for studying topological magnetic states.
main_problem: The paper aims to engineer and control tunable p-wave magnetism in a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic bilayer system without relying on strong spin-orbit coupling or external driving.
main_result: The in-plane relative shift between the two magnetic layers acts as a symmetry-breaking knob, generating tunable p-wave spin splitting and associated spin responses in the ground state.
method: The study uses a symmetry-guided approach, mapping the system onto an effective bond-modulated square lattice and analyzing the corresponding Hubbard model via mean-field theory.
model_or_system: The physical system is an AB-stacked bilayer of antiferromagnetic square lattices. The theoretical framework involves a Hubbard model analyzed in a mean-field treatment, allowing for the study of various magnetic phases.
key_observables: p-wave spin-splitting strength ($S_p$), p-wave order direction ($	heta_p$), and the charge-to-spin conversion tensor ($\chi$) related to the Edelstein effect.
important_parameters: The in-plane relative displacement ($\eta$) between the two layers is the primary control parameter, alongside the magnetic ordering angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field theory for the Hubbard model and assumes the system remains fully compensated (zero net magnetization) due to preserved symmetries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup using the in-plane shift ($\eta$), show spin-resolved electronic structure contours, and map out the continuous tunability of the p-wave order ($S_p$) and spin response ($\chi$) as functions of $\eta$ and $	heta$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the symmetry-protected mechanism for generating p-wave splitting via geometric displacement. It then develops the theoretical framework by mapping to an effective lattice and analyzing the Hubbard model in mean-field theory to predict phase diagrams and measurable spin responses.
why_interesting: The concept of using geometric displacement ($\eta$) as a tunable knob to induce exotic magnetic order (p-wave magnetism) in an equilibrium state is highly relevant for designing novel quantum materials and spintronic devices.
